jd_snippet: We are looking for a skilled and motivated Data Scientist to analyze complex datasets, develop machine learning models, and generate actionable insights that support business decision-making. The ideal candidate should have strong knowledge of statistics, machine learning, data analysis, and programming, along with the ability to communicate technical findings effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

questions.answer: I started my career at thesis and then moved on to flip-flit as senior data, so at this  we had opportunity to work on more complex long-skilled columns.  I read a team that developed a project recommendation using collaborative data.  What attracted me to data science is the combination. | Follow-up: [No answer detected]
questions.feedback: Interesting, so you started in academia and then moved to industry, and it's the combination of data science that really drew you in?

questions.question: I noticed you worked on a product recommendation engine at Flipkart.
questions.feedback: Interesting, so you picked up on that specific project. Can you tell me more about what you liked about working on that product recommendation engine?

questions.question: How did you decide which algorithms to use for the product recommendation engine, and what metrics did you use to evaluate its performance?
questions.feedback: Interesting that you didn't mention which algorithms you used for the product recommendation engine. Can you walk me through your thought process on that?

questions.question: What kind of data processing techniques did you use to process the 10TB+ of daily user event data at Flipkart, and how did you ensure the models were scalable and performant?
questions.feedback: That's a big data processing task. Can you walk me through your approach to processing that large dataset?

questions.question: How did you leverage your knowledge of deep learning and NLP to develop the customer review sentiment analysis model using BERT and PyTorch at Flipkart?
questions.feedback: That's a great start, but I'm a bit surprised you didn't dive deeper into your experience with BERT and PyTorch. Can you walk me through how you fine-tuned the BERT model for this specific task and what kind of improvements you saw in the sentiment analysis results?

questions.question: Can you walk me through your approach to handling class imbalance in the churn prediction model you built at TCS?
questions.feedback: That's a pretty important question for a churn prediction model. Can you take a stab at it now?

questions.question: What aspects of this Data Scientist role at our company excite you the most?
questions.feedback: That's a pretty open-ended question, and I'm not seeing a clear answer. Can you help me understand what specific aspects of this role excite you?
